newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan business group welcomes Bhutto's fall.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan business group welcomes Bhutto's fall.

text.p: The Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce and Industry said on Tuesday it hoped President Farooq Leghari's dismissal of Benazir Bhutto's government would augur well for the battered economy.
"The president's decision, though quite late, has finally ended the uncertainty on the political front," the federation's president Senator Ilyas Bilour told reporters in Karachi.
Bilour said Leghari's action was likely to improve investor confidence, whatever the political implications.

He urged the new caretaker government led by Meraj Khalid to prosecute corrupt businessmen, bureaucrats and politicians, restore the credibility of institutions, and sack government employees appointed on political grounds.
"Corruption and over-employment was a burden on the economy. The new set-up should rectify the situation to restore confidence among businessmen," he said.
Leghari named Khalid to lead a nine-member interim cabinet empowered to lead Pakistan into a general election that the president said should take place on February 3, 1997.
Bilour demanded that extra powers given to the police and paramilitary rangers in Karachi since 1992 should be scrapped immediately to help restore normality in the southern city.
"The civilian status of Karachi should immediately be restored so that the image of a terrorist city projected by the former goverment is done away with," Bilour said.

Bilour asked the new government to reconnect cellular telephone and pager services in Karachi that were cut off by the Bhutto government in July 1995 in a bid to disrupt the communications of the militant Mohajir National Movement.
